messages.subject: Two-tier model and DIF
parts:
Hello Phil and group,

First, a huge thank you to Phil for the fantastic and huge job in developing this package and for the amazing support provided via this community. This is of immense value in my research, thank you.

I would like to inquire about my model. I would be much grateful and appreciate any help with it.

I have identified the following two-tier (graded response) model as the best to fit my polytomous personality-type data.
dif_model <- mirt.model("
G1 = 1-7
G2 = 8-28
F1 = 8-14
F2 = 15-21
F3 = 22-28
COV = G1*G2
")
Q1: Would this model be identified, considering that G1 is a general factor model which is assumed to correlate with G2, but has no lower-order factors loading on its items (whereas G2 has)? In my analyses, this had the better fit compared to bifactor, multidimensional, and unidimensional models.

Q2: I would like to test for DIF. What is the best strategy to do so? My attempts:
(a) run this exact model via the multipleGroup() function, including a set of anchor items plus freely estimating means and variances.
(b) same as (a) but using bifactor instead of multipleGroup().
(c) forget about general factors, and only test for DIF via a multidimensional model accounting for four correlated lower-order factors (i.e., F1[previously G1], F2, F3, F4).
(d) forget about the multidimensional structure and run a series of four unidimensional DIF analyses (i.e., one per factor, namely F1[previously G1], F2, F3, F4).

Q3: I have 3 groups to test for DIF. Would the 'classic' approach still be valid, or would you recommend breaking it down in multiple pairwise comparisons (e.g., run a multigroup analysis accounting for group1 vs. group2, then group2 vs. group3, and group1 vs. group3)?

Thanks anyone in advance for your attention and support you might be able to provide.
 
Emanuele
